answer: A farm cannot fake the aggregate without controlling every key it names, thus paying the vault bond on all of them and exposing each to the pearl slash. Attestations are aggregated into one signature over 15 distinct keys, and the aggregate must verify against each key's registered public value. Because the knoll audit verifies the aggregate, a single forged member invalidates the whole batch. A 456 account operation therefore ties up 31 million dollars of idle capital. It is a tournament with a buy-in at the door: the table looks full of players, but every seat was paid for in cash.
